summary: Author and test cyclic clips at the wrap as a boundary condition, checking pose and, where desired, first-derivative continuity under the exported interpolation and runtime loop mode.
objective: A repeated cycle preserves intended rhythm without a pose pop, root jump, duplicate hold or velocity kink that the selected style did not request.
applies_when: A walk, idle, mechanism or environmental motion repeats.
A clip uses LINEAR, STEP or CUBICSPLINE interpolation across an export/runtime boundary.
intent_signals: fix a popping glTF animation loop
test pose and velocity at animation seam
make reverse and ping-pong loops stable
example_prompts: Loop a breathing motion without a pause caused by duplicate endpoints.
Preserve a deliberate stepped robot cycle while rejecting an accidental root jump.
negative_signals: Assuming matching first and last values guarantee smooth velocity.
Treating zeroSlopeAtStart/End as proof that arbitrary exported endpoints form a seamless loop.
not_for: Root-displacement accumulation without a root-motion ownership policy.

principles: A loop seam joins the clip’s end to its start. Decide separately whether the style requires value continuity, first-derivative continuity, a deliberate step, or ping-pong reversal.
Inspect the exported clip, not only Blender playback. Sampling, optimization, clip duration and interpolation can change which endpoint values and tangents the runtime evaluates.
A duplicate terminal pose can be useful for authored timing but may add a hold when the runtime duration also wraps to the first pose. Establish the exact duration and endpoint convention per clip.
implementation: In Blender, compare the start pose to the pose one cycle later and compare root displacement and tangent intent. Mark deliberate discontinuities instead of smoothing them by default.

Inspect glTF sampler times and interpolation. For CUBICSPLINE, evaluate both sides of the seam with the transported tangents; for LINEAR compare segment slopes; for STEP require the exact intentional jump. Configure AnimationAction loop mode and duration explicitly.

Test forward, negative timeScale and ping-pong independently. Record a small seam window of transforms/morph weights and derived finite-difference velocities; keep root displacement evaluation under the root-motion profile.
observable_checks: Immediately before and after wrap, all channels satisfy the declared value tolerance; smooth loops also satisfy the declared finite-difference velocity tolerance.
The loop cadence contains neither an unintended extra terminal hold nor a missing beat at the seam.
Forward, reverse and ping-pong fixtures each exhibit the declared boundary behavior, including an intentionally stepped control clip.

creative_affordances: Seams may be invisible, deliberately percussive, elastic, stepped or asymmetrical.
Different channels in one clip may intentionally use different continuity classes.
known_limits: Three.js endpoint slope controls influence interpolation ending behavior but do not certify authored seam continuity.
Finite-difference tolerances depend on scale, frame interval and intended style.
No clip export or loop playback was run.

claims.statement: glTF 2.0 animation samplers support LINEAR, STEP and CUBICSPLINE interpolation and clamp output to the nearest endpoint outside the input range.
claims.scope: glTF 2.0.1 sampler behavior; runtime loop wrapping is outside the core file specification.

source_refs.locator: Section 3.11 Animations and Appendix C interpolation

claims.statement: Three.js AnimationAction exposes LoopOnce, LoopRepeat and LoopPingPong modes, wraps or clamps local time by loop state, and has configurable zeroSlopeAtStart and zeroSlopeAtEnd flags.
claims.scope: Live Three.js AnimationAction API; seam quality still requires observation.
